story_title: German State Elections: Merz's CDU Defeat & AfD Gains
block_title: german state elections: merz's cdu defeat & afd gains
block_sentences: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has cancelled a trip to the United Nations and cleared his calendar to deal with potential aftershocks after his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) suffered its worst result in a state election since World War II, barely clearing the threshold to enter parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won 38.3 percent of the vote in the state, ahead of the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) on 35.4 percent, while the CDU secured just 4.9 percent.
In Berlin, the hard-left Die Linke emerged as the largest party with 25.3 percent, followed by the CDU at 19 percent and the AfD at 16.3 percent.

Merz described the result as a 'disaster' but struck a defiant note, rejecting any retreat from his government’s reform agenda and insisting that difficult measures are more urgent due to Germany’s economic and political problems.
He said in a statement that 'what needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness, and patience'.
Calls have emerged over the past fortnight, including from within his own party, for him to step down, although no top-level allies have called publicly for his departure.
The AfD’s national co-leader, Tino Chrupalla, told ZDF television that the chancellor's statement was 'more than feeble' and called on him to resign.

story_title: Russia's wartime parliamentary election and aftermath
block_title: russia's wartime parliamentary election and aftermath
block_sentences: Russia’s ruling United Russia party has won a parliamentary election marred by the exclusion of opposition candidates and drone attacks, securing 57.5% of the vote and 355 seats out of 450, according to election officials.

The vote, the first since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, was held in occupied territories and excluded the only registered anti-war party, Yabloko, which was barred from the ballot by the Supreme Court.

International observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe were barred from monitoring the election, with the Russian Foreign Ministry accusing the body of “double standards”.

Opposition parties reported that their observers were turned away from polling stations and that some were arrested, while violations included sealed ballot boxes being opened and voters being denied paper ballots.
The election took place as Ukraine launched a massive drone attack on Moscow, killing at least three people in the region and two in the occupied Kherson area, including an election official.

Authorities in Kyiv denounced the voting in Russian-held areas as illegal and urged foreign governments not to recognize the result, while the European Union called the action a “blatant violation of international law”.
Russia vowed to “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv in response to the drone attacks, accusing Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens”.

story_title: White House bans CNN, MS NOW, Politico
block_title: white house bans cnn, ms now, politico
block_sentences: US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, a move that prompted immediate denunciations from press freedom advocates and legal experts who warned the action was likely unconstitutional.

The outlets reported that their reporters were denied entry and had their press badges confiscated by the Secret Service on Saturday morning, with Trump citing what he called “constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS” as the justification.

Trump did not identify specific stories that prompted the ban, saying instead that it was based on “cumulative stories over the last few years,” and he warned that other outlets could face a similar fate.

The White House Correspondents’ Association condemned the ban, stating that the constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference and that press access is not a privilege for journalists.
The Associated Press, which was previously barred from the Oval Office and Air Force One over its refusal to use the name “Gulf of America,” said it supported the news organizations banned this week.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico said they were filing a lawsuit to protect their First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes.

Legal experts noted that the president does not possess the authority to arbitrarily ban entire outlets from the White House based on the content they publish, and a press freedom group expected the ban to be struck down by the courts.

Some residents in Greenland's capital, Nuuk, remain skeptical about closer ties with Washington.
